newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco lists credit firm CREDOR on the bourse.
newsitem.headline: Morocco lists credit firm CREDOR on the bourse.

text.p: Morocco listed on Tuesday a leading private credit firm CREDOR on the Casablanca stock exchange, a bourse spokeswoman said.
"CREDOR is the 47th firm to be listed on the bourse...It closed at 397 dirhams per share, up 3.0 percent over its initial price," the spokeswoman said.
Credit Domestic Rapide (CREDOR) floated last week 240,000 shares worth 92.4 million dirhams ($10.5 million) on the stock exchange. It was offered for 385 dirhams per share, a stockbroker said.
"According to the first estimate, the firm was 17.5 times oversubscribed...The demand reached 4.2 million," he said.

Established in 1987 in Casablanca, Credit Domestic Rapide (CREDOR), has a capital of 120 million dirhams and expects a net profit of 55 million dirhams by end 1996 compared with 45.5 million in 1995, Casablanca Finance Intermediation said.
Specialised in domestic consumer credit, CREDOR holds an average 16 percent of Morocco's market share, it said.
"CREDOR is the first private firm to be floated on the Casablanca bourse since the government launched its privatisation programme in 1993," said a broker at the Casablanca-based Upline Securities.
The government programme includes 114 state-owned enterprises to be sold between 1993 and end 1998. It already privatised 46 companies including two credit companies.
"Credor is implementing an offensive commercial strategy which aims at doubling its credit portfolio by the year 2000 and reinforcing its position in the personal loan segment," the broker said.
A total 11 state-owned firms were floated on the stock exchange, including Samir Morocco's main oil refinery, since 1993.
The 67-year-old bourse has reached 73.3 billion dirhams as market capitalisation on Tuesday, the bourse said.
